nodes.name: Pt-mem Preparation
nodes.procedure: Nanoporous PTFE membrane was cleaned by sonication in acetone and methanol (30 min each), rinsed with DI water, dried, and UV-ozone treated for 5 min. Then, 400 nm of Pt was deposited using magnetron ion sputtering.

unit_operations.name: Surface Activation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: exposed to UV generated ozone for 5 min to clean the surface

unit_operations.name: Metal Deposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Pt (99.999%) was deposited onto the nanoporous PTFE membrane using the CIS400 magnetron ion sputtering instrument

nodes.source_text: A nanoporous PTFE membrane (20 nm pore size) was used ... to form Pt-mem with an effective thickness of 400 nm.

nodes.name: Au-mem Preparation
nodes.procedure: Au (99.999%) was deposited onto the PTFE membrane with 400 nm thickness using magnetron ion sputtering to serve as a carrier for other catalysts.
nodes.source_text: Au (99.999%) was deposited onto the PTFE membrane with 400 nm thickness to form the membrane electrode carrier for other catalysts.

nodes.name: RuO2 Ink Preparation
nodes.procedure: 4 mg of RuO2 powder dispersed in 1.5 mL of deionized water and ethanol (4:1 volume ratio) with 40 μL of Nafion solution, followed by ultrasonication for 1 h.
nodes.source_text: The catalyst ink was prepared by dispersing Pt and the metal oxides (4 mg) ... in a mixture of 1.5 mL of deionized water and ethanol ... with 40 μL of Nafion solution ... After ultrasonication for 1 h

nodes.procedure: 3 μL of RuO2 ink was dropped onto the Au-coated PTFE membrane. After drying, 3 μL of Pt ink was added to the same interface.

unit_operations.name: Oxide Layer Coating
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: 3 μL of the metal oxide was dropped on electrodes firstly.

nodes.source_text: As for bimetallic interfaces, 3 μL of the metal oxide was dropped on electrodes firstly. After drying, 3 μL of Pt was added to ensure the same loadings on two types of electrodes.

nodes.name: Microchannel Cell Fabrication
nodes.procedure: Bonding glass slide and silicon wafer at 300-500 C. Spin-coating negative photoresist at 3000 rpm, baking at 100 C for 1.5 min. UV patterning and developing. Wet etching silicon with KOH. Laser perforation of glass slide 2. Final anodic bonding to form glass-silicon-glass sandwich structure.

unit_operations.name: Anodic Bonding
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: At 300-500 C, the metal ions in the glass slide moved toward the positive side... resulting in extremely high bond strength.

unit_operations.name: Spin-coating
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Negative photoresists were spin-coated onto silicon wafers at 3000 rpm and then baked at 100 C for 1.5 min.

unit_operations.name: Silicon Etching
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Single crystal silicon was etched using KOH until the glass sheet layer was exposed.
